science.title: Resveratrol exerts neuroprotective properties by modulating brain SIRT1 gene expression in lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation in rats
science.description: Neuroinflammation is responsible for many neurodegenerative diseases and conditions. In this study, neuroprotective effect of resveratrol was aimed to be investigated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammatory model. Special interest was focused on SIRT1 gene expression, which acts on the regulation of proteins involved in cellular homeostasis. Rats were used and single dose of 1 mg/kg body weight LPS and/or 10 mg/kg body weight resveratrol were given. EX-527, as a specific inhibitor of SIRT1 was also tested. The effects of LPS and/or resveratrol on spatial learning and memory were assessed using the Morris water maze test. SIRT1 gene expression was studied by q-real time-PCR in brain tissue. Changes in malondialdehyde (MDA), reduced glutathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) levels were also compared. No significant changes were observed on cognitive functions among the groups. SIRT1 gene expression in brain tissue was significantly higher in the Res + LPS group than in the other groups, while it was significantly lower in the EX527 + LPS group than in all other groups. MDA levels and SOD activity were found to be higher in the Res and Res + LPS groups compared to the other groups. In histopathological findings, the number of degenerative neurons in hippocampal tissues was significantly higher in the LPS-administered group than in the control group, and significantly lower in the resveratrol-administered group than in the LPS group. Results suggested that resveratrol would be effective in ameliorating the degenerative effects caused by LPS in brain tissue and this effect might be due to increased SIRT1 gene expression.

science.title: Physicists entangle quantum memories across a record-breaking 420 km
science.description: Optical fibers are already the backbone of global communication systems. Recently, however, physicists have started to explore how their functionality could be boosted further by conveying information via entangled quantum particles—potentially enabling instantaneous exchanges of information across vast distances. Such a system could eventually be the basis of a future 'quantum internet,' offering a level of security and computing power beyond anything possible today.

science.title: Rethinking how we name and classify our human ancestors following recent evolutionary discoveries
science.description:
Recent advances in our understanding of human evolution challenge the way we currently name and classify our ancestors, according to new research from Monash University.
The research, published in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology, argues that we need a rethink, and proposes reclassifying all species of humans and our closely related fossil relatives that have lived in the past 4-5 million years as part of the Homo genus.
Human evolution is often presented as a straightforward progression through distinct species, from ape-like ancestors, through Australopithecus and earlier members of Homo, culminating in Homo Sapiens that live today.

science.title: Structural snapshots reveal key steps in switching on DNA replication
science.description: Every time a cell divides, it must accurately copy its entire genetic instruction manual. Before this process can begin, cells load their DNA-copying motor—a complex of six subunits known as the MCM2-7 helicase—onto DNA. However, this motor is deliberately kept inactive to prevent replication from starting at the wrong time.
